@coll09 draws a relational comparison between knowledge and power. The point is that knowledge will enable an individual to obtain what they want out of life. She then argues that historically, knowledge in black communities has been suppressed. What Collins means by suppressing knowledge however, occurs through the suppression of the intellectual output of black women in broader American society.

Namely the intellectual views of black women on poverty, oppression, independence etc. However, these knowledge domains, largely influential in formal education, are not central to more important knowledge domains. It is these other knowledge domains that are central to the flourishing of a culture and an individual. The source of these other knowledge domains is first in the home for it is in the home where we learn who we are, what matters, and most importantly, that we are loved and desired.
